title: DA 2PLSM Measurements with Genetically Encoded Probes
author: Enrico Zampese
materials: With the imaging software, preliminary adjust power and image acquisition settings (it is recommended starting from lower settings and increasing laser power and/or gain if needed) and start imaging in “live” mode. The 2P excitation wavelength adopted for the probes mentioned above, all based on GFP, is 920nm. Other kinds of probe might yield better results with different excitation wavelengths.
Discard slices and waste solutions according to institutional protocols.
Turn off all the equipment according to instructions.
Export data and proceed with image analysis.

steps.title: Prepare and hold brain slices
steps.instruction: Obtain brain slices expressing GES according to the established protocol and keep them at room temperature in a chamber containing aCSF continuously bubbled with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ until the experiment.

steps.title: Power on 2PLSM station
steps.instruction: Turn on the 2PLSM working station, including the heated stage and the controlling computer.

steps.title: Start aCSF perfusion
steps.instruction: Run aCSF through the peristaltic pump into the microscope chamber, ensure the chamber outlet removes solution at the same rate into a waste collector; if available, use a vacuum‑based outlet to help prevent overflow.

steps.title: Set chamber temperature
steps.instruction: Insert a temperature probe into the chamber solution and allow the system to warm until the chamber reaches 32–33 °C.

steps.title: Transfer slice to imaging chamber
steps.instruction: When the chamber temperature approaches the target, move one slice from the holding chamber into the imaging chamber, adjust its position, and gently place a slice holder on top without covering any region of interest.

steps.title: Check GES expression
steps.instruction: Using the eyepieces and LED illumination with a low‑magnification objective, verify correct GES expression and adjust the stage so the region of interest can be easily accessed.

steps.title: Switch to 60× immersion lens
steps.instruction: Replace the objective with a 60× immersion lens, visualize the slice surface, turn off the LED, and activate the 2PLSM settings.

steps.title: Optimize imaging settings
steps.instruction: Identify a region to image and set imaging parameters: zoom 8, 64 × 64 pixel image size, 8 µs dwell time, whole‑field spiral scan yielding ~40 frames s⁻¹; adjust field of view, resolution, and frame rate as needed.

steps.title: Set laser power and gain
steps.instruction: Adjust laser power and PMT gain so baseline fluorescence is bright but below saturation (saturation > 4095 units, target baseline ≈ 1000 units). With the laser shutter closed, acquire a background image (~100 units) for later subtraction.

steps.title: Allow slice equilibration
steps.instruction: Wait at least 10–15 min after placing the slice and lowering the 60× objective before starting any experiment to let the slice stabilize at the chamber temperature.

steps.title: Select acquisition mode
steps.instruction: Decide whether to perform time‑lapse acquisitions (for slow pharmacological effects) or continuous Brightness‑Over‑Time acquisitions (for fast acute stimulation).

steps.title: Perform in situ calibration
steps.instruction: If a semi‑quantitative approach is desired, estimate the maximum fluorescence for the slice by an in situ calibration of the probe’s dynamic range.

steps.title: Configure time‑lapse acquisition
steps.instruction: For slow effects, acquire 60 frames over ~15 s every 10 min; average each series to obtain one time‑point in the time‑lapse.

steps.title: Configure continuous acquisition
steps.instruction: For fast effects, use PrairieView’s Brightness‑Over‑Time mode to record continuously.

steps.title: Measure Fmax
steps.instruction: Wash in aCSF containing a saturating concentration of the relevant neurotransmitter (e.g., 100 µM acetylcholine chloride for GRABACh3.0); the GES reaches saturation within ~5 min. Continue Brightness‑Over‑Time acquisition until a stable maximum fluorescence level is obtained.

steps.title: Discard slice and clean
steps.instruction: After Fmax measurements, discard the slice and clean the imaging chamber.

steps.title: Wash tubing and optics
steps.instruction: Thoroughly wash tubing, microscope chamber, slice holder, and the 60× objective with water, then with 10 % ethanol, and finally rinse again with water.

steps.title: Restrict iris diaphragm
steps.instruction: With the region of interest positioned, close the iris diaphragm to isolate a sub‑region within the GES‑expressing area.

steps.title: Place stimulation electrode
steps.instruction: Place the tip of the tungsten bipolar electrode onto the slice at the border of the small light circle generated by the restricted iris; keep stimulation location and intensity consistent across experiments.
